html:
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 at Palashi in Bengal, where the East India Company under Robert Clive beat Siraj ud-Daulah, the nawab of Bengal. It gave the Company control of Bengal and began British rule in India.

The year before, Siraj had captured the Company's town of Calcutta. Clive retook it and then plotted with men around the nawab: his army commander Mir Jafar and the bankers of the house of Jagat Seth.

On the day, Clive had about 3,000 men against a nawab's army many times larger, with French gunners. A rainstorm soaked the nawab's powder while the British kept theirs covered. Mir Jafar's troops held back. The nawab's army broke, and Siraj fled and was soon killed.

Mir Jafar became nawab and paid the Company and its officers huge sums. The Company then won at Buxar in 1764 and in 1765 took the right to collect Bengal's revenue. Bengal's wealth paid for later conquests. Five years later came the Bengal famine of 1770.
sum: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 at Palashi in Bengal, where the East India Company under Robert Clive beat Siraj ud-Daulah, the nawab of Bengal. It gave the Company control of Bengal and began British rule in India.
